definition: Transient means lasting or staying only a short time.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word transient. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know transient should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The hostel's transient guests leave notes in the kitchen — half thanks, half directions — signed with first names only.
Visiting is the mildest rung — a visiting scholar has a return ticket and a home campus waiting; a transient guest checks out with no promise of coming back.
Rootless goes further than transient: a transient crew stays briefly and moves on to the next stop, while a rootless one belongs nowhere at all, with no base to go back to.

Passing marks the moment of going by: a passing shower, a passing glance — here and gone almost at once. It is briefer and more of-the-moment than transient, which can cover weeks or a season: short in the life of the thing, but long enough to live in.

Temporary means in place for a limited time by design — the end is planned from the start, written into the contract or posted on the sign. Transient things leave of their own accord: guests, moods, symptoms, with no clause deciding when. Temporary is scheduled; transient simply passes.

The mayor's new budget doubles transit funding without naming a single project.
Transient means lasting or staying only a short time.
The clinic's discharge sheet divides symptoms into two columns.
Dizziness on standing, it says, is transient: expect it, sit down, let it pass — it visits and moves on like weather.
Numbness that stays past an hour belongs in the other column, the one printed with a phone number.
Transient is the working word because it means lasting or staying only a short time — the emphasis falls on the leaving.
It promises nothing about how the stay ends or what it meant, only that it will be brief.
That neutrality is why nurses, physicists, and innkeepers all reach for the same adjective.
Transient is the level-headed word for what stays briefly — guests, symptoms, moods, populations — equally at home on a chart and in a poem.
Its unit-mate evanescent is the rapturous one: an evanescent thing dissolves even as you watch.
Say transient when the point is a short stay; say evanescent when the point is the vanishing itself.

Every few years, when winter rain reaches the desert basin, a lake appears where maps show only salt flats.
The lake is transient, and everything that comes to it seems to know.
Shorebirds arrive within days and feed around the clock; brine shrimp hatch from eggs that have waited in the crust, sometimes for a decade.
The water may last six weeks or six months, and no forecast can say which -- it goes when evaporation and the sand decide.
By midsummer the birds have moved on, the shoreline is a chalk line of salt, and the basin returns to being a map's small lie.
